question: Q03 what platforms were never tested - measured on Linux, not asserted

windows_baseline_for_comparison.note: carried figure from the pinned baseline; NOT re-run by this unit

deltas.collected_delta_note: UNVERIFIED: more tests collected on Linux than the Windows baseline reports; parametrisation over discovered files is the likely driver but the cause was not investigated. Settling experiment: pytest --collect-only -q on both platforms and diff the node id lists.

root_cause.verdict: CONFIRMED for 21 of 24 failures (all in platform/routing)
root_cause.mechanism: platform/routing/index.py:55 sets HOME = Path(os.environ.get('ROUTING_HOME') or Path.home()), and index.py:93-97 binds skills/agents/commands under that HOME. The capability corpus under test is therefore the OPERATOR's LIVE ~/.claude harness, not a committed fixture.
root_cause.measurement: Windows ~/.claude: agents=27 commands=71 skills=79. Linux ~/.claude: agents=0 commands=0 skills=0. Linux indexed 383 records; the test's own positive-form guard asserts >800 and fired: 'corpus implausibly small (383); the walk is probably broken'.
root_cause.consequence: The Phase 8 capability count and every derived precision/recall and bytes-per-query figure are machine-specific and not reproducible in CI or on any other host. This also structurally explains the missing platform/ CI lane: these tests cannot pass on a runner with no ~/.claude harness, so the absence of CI is forced by the design rather than merely forgotten.
root_cause.credit_where_due: The tests are well designed: they assert the POSITIVE form (N of N, plus an explicit implausibly-small floor) which is exactly why the coupling surfaced instead of passing vacuously.
root_cause.available_fix_seam: ROUTING_HOME already exists at index.py:55 and no test sets it. Pointing it at a committed fixture corpus would make the lane hermetic (ci-hygiene.md 2) and unblock a platform/ CI lane.

control.probe: python3 -m pytest platform/plugin -q on the SAME Linux interpreter
control.meaning: a disjoint subpackage passes cleanly, so the 24 failures are localised - a blanket 'the build breaks on Linux' claim is REFUTED

scope_limits: the 3 non-routing failures were not individually triaged
no macOS run was attempted - no macOS host exists on this estate
the Windows baseline was carried, not re-measured by this unit
run over /mnt/c (Windows filesystem) so wall-clock is not a fair perf comparison
